sources.title: Introducing Perceptron Mk1
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27, 2026, including visual inspection of all three original benchmark tables. The May 12 launch identifies exact API model perceptron-mk1 as the first closed Perceptron-family model. Tables contain prices and benchmark scores, with no Mk1 total or active parameter count or named base checkpoint.

sources.title: Perceptron Mk1 model guide
sources.evidence: Fresh direct Markdown retrieval succeeded October 27, 2026 (the web reader could not fetch this URL). Exact perceptron-mk1 guide remains closed-source with text/image/video inputs, text output, 32K context and optional reasoning. It reports no parameter count, architecture or named base; tool-calling guidance points to Mk1.5.

sources.title: Mk1 Chat Completions API reference
sources.evidence: The tool_calling_not_supported error example explicitly identifies perceptron-mk1. Shared schema fields require a capable model and do not confer tool support on Mk1. Direct Markdown retrieval succeeded.

sources.title: Perceptron Mk1 changelog
sources.evidence: Explicit May 12, 2026 Mk1 launch entry corroborates the original announcement, including image/video, reasoning and 32K context. Direct Markdown retrieval succeeded.

sources.title: Terms of Use
sources.evidence: July 10, 2026 terms retain Perceptron ownership and grant restricted service access; weight access or self-hosting requires enterprise rights. Supports a descriptive Proprietary classification, not an open-source license.

sources.title: Mk1 MCP integration
sources.evidence: MCP exposes vision operations to external assistants. It does not document Mk1 deciding to invoke tools itself. Direct Markdown retrieval succeeded.

sources.title: Introducing Perceptron Mk1.5
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27, 2026. September 25 release adds native audio and tool calling; Mk1 comparisons report performance and end-to-end latency on one H100, not parameter counts. It does not identify Mk1 as a variant of a named counted checkpoint. Added modalities also preclude assuming identical whole-model structure across Mk1 and Mk1.5.

sources.title: Teaching VLMs to think visually
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27, 2026. The June 18 study explicitly labels its experimental base Isaac, 9B, in the training pipeline; the text contains no Mk1 identification. Its SFT/RL experiments cannot establish Mk1 size or base lineage.

sources.title: Composing Weight and Data Sparsity in MoE
sources.evidence: Freshly reopened October 27, 2026. January 21 research upcycles Qwen3 0.6B/1.7B bases into experimental MoEs; its extended-training table labels 18B-A3B experiments, Isaac 0.2 2B and InternVL3.5-20B-A4B. No Mk1 row or named Mk1 lineage connects those counts to this model.

sources.title: Isaac 0.5: Percepts Scale Control
sources.evidence: Fresh web reopening October 27, 2026 succeeded. Also inspected the 52-page PDF fetched at 15:57:40 UTC in the primary-source cache, including section 2.2, section 3.1 and a rendered Table 11 (page 26). Mk1 is only the proprietary annotation model. Table 11 explicitly assigns 36B total/2.5B active to Isaac 0.5; other comparison tables omit Mk1. A separate direct refetch returned HTTP 403, so no successful local refetch is claimed.

sources.title: Perceptron Mk1 API model page
sources.evidence: Provider documentation specifies its exact Mk1 route at 32,768 context tokens, agreeing with Perceptron’s nominal 32K. Used only for route-level integer precision, not as model-architecture or original-release evidence.

sources.title: Perceptron releases 35B Mk1.5 model for embodied agents
sources.evidence: Secondary lead reopened October 27, 2026. Despite its headline, the article explicitly attributes 35B to rohanpaul_ai and says the official announcement leaves parameter count unstated. The claim concerns Mk1.5, not Mk1. Its linked X post returned HTTP 403. Used only to trace and reject this lead, not as a specification.

sources.title: Perceptron Mk1 tokenizer identity record
sources.evidence: Search lead reopened October 27, 2026. Reports a Qwen-like tokenizer fingerprint measured August 21. Tokenizer reuse does not identify an exact base checkpoint, tensor structure or size; this is not a developer lineage statement or a total/active parameter measurement.

name.note: Exact public name for API ID perceptron-mk1; distinct from Mk1.5.

developer.note: Developer announcement and service terms identify Perceptron.

family.note: The launch explicitly names the Perceptron model family, distinct from its Isaac series.

release_date.note: Actual public launch and same-day API availability; not inferred from a provider listing or catalog timestamp.

open_weights.note: Mk1 is closed source and proprietary. Negotiated enterprise access does not constitute an open-weight release.

license.note: Descriptive classification supported by restricted service/enterprise terms and the report’s explicit proprietary Mk1 designation.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 searches for Mk1 parameters, billion/35B, base-model lineage and later research comparisons found no supported nominal total. Reopened developer sources name no counted Mk1 base. Isaac 0.5 is a distinct checkpoint; the third-party 35B claim concerns Mk1.5, and tokenizer fingerprints establish no count.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh searches for exact Mk1 active/activated counts and later original comparison tables found no stated convention. Launch tables and Mk1.5 comparisons provide no count; Isaac 0.5 Table 11 has explicit active/total columns but no Mk1 row. Its 2.5B active count and the older MoE experiments cannot transfer to Mk1.

architecture.note: Vision-language describes function, not topology. Research describes other models; no exact Mk1 Transformer, dense or MoE specification is established.

context_window.note: Developer states nominal 32K; OpenRouter specifies 32,768 for this exact route. Retained as a documented API limit, not independently measured capacity.

modalities.note: Exact Mk1 guide lists these modalities. Grounding annotations are serialized output; audio support belongs to Mk1.5.

reasoning.note: Mk1 documents optional thinking through vision_config.enable_thinking.

tool_call.note: Exact Mk1 API error rejects declared tools and tool-call histories. MCP makes Mk1 callable by other agents; that does not make Mk1 tool-capable.

description.value: Vision-language model for image and video understanding, spatial grounding, and embodied reasoning, with optional thinking.
description.note: Replaces the unsupported planning/tool-use wording with documented visual tasks and optional reasoning.

patch.description: Vision-language model for image and video understanding, spatial grounding, and embodied reasoning, with optional thinking.
patch.notes: Mk1 supports optional reasoning but not function calling; MCP lets other agents invoke its vision capabilities. Total and active parameter counts, architecture and a named base model remain undisclosed. Isaac and Mk1.5 counts do not establish Mk1 specifications. The developer specifies 32K context; its OpenRouter route specifies 32,768 tokens.

sources.label: Composing Weight and Data Sparsity in MoE

summary: Fresh October 27 parameter re-audit retained undisclosed total and active counts after reopening the launch tables, exact guide, Mk1.5 comparisons, training studies and Isaac 0.5 report, plus bounded searches for later disclosures and named lineage. Isaac counts, the third-party Mk1.5 35B claim and tokenizer fingerprints do not establish Mk1 counts. Explicit null parameter patches added; the other 12 field assessments are unchanged.
